title: TESS dips of the old dusty star G4466 in 2022 need rigid occulting screens faster than 7 stellar radii per day; on circular orbits this dust is within 0.16-0.78 au, where new hot dust appeared
abstract: Question: where is the dust that makes the deep, aperiodic dips of old field dwarfs? The dust location of Gaia20cdd is disputed (below 0.3 au or 2.5-4 au), and the only kinematic limit assumed one straight occulter edge. Method: we made our own photometry of TESS 31x31-pixel cutouts of the old extreme-dust dimmer G4466 (Gaia DR3 4466400095283726080) in 2020, 2022 and 2024, with 6-8 same-field comparison stars. We fitted the resolved dips with rigid rectangular screens that move at fixed speeds across a limb-darkened disc, checked the fits with a global optimiser and six analysis variants, and compared the dip widths with 15,941 random screen shapes. We also derived a bound that holds for any rigid screen pattern: the flux change is at most the light of the crescent that the moving disc uncovers. Results: in TESS sector 52 (2022 May-June), inside the months in which NEOWISE saw new 1050 K dust appear, G4466 had many dips of 3-15 percent with 1-3 hour walls; 2020 and 2024 were much quieter. Three isolated events give the same best speed, 9.5 stellar radii per day, and 3-sigma lower limits of 7.05-7.41 per day (variants: 6.66-8.29). No random screen shape makes dips this deep and narrow below 6.0-7.3 stellar radii per day. The speed is at least 43 km/s (R* = 0.75 R_sun) to 70 km/s (Gaia single-star radius 1.23 R_sun). On circular orbits the dust is within 0.42 au (single 0.75 R_sun component), 0.78 au (circumbinary) or 0.16 au (single star); the best fit gives 0.09-0.23 au. Dust at several au is excluded for G4466. For circular orbits, the blackbody temperature at the occulter orbit is 650-870 K for the single-star parameters, close to the new hot dust; this links the 2022 dips to fresh dust made close to the star. The crescent bound alone gives only 6.5-10.7 km/s because the dips are shallow. Limitations: no spectrum, and G4466 can be a binary, so the radius is uncertain; screens that form or clear in place within hours are not covered; the shape test is an empirical envelope of rectangles and Gaussian blobs; fits have chi2/dof 1.6-3.5 (red noise); one star and one season; G2874 shows only slow TESS changes and Gaia20cdd is too blended for this method. display.caption: Three isolated TESS dips of G4466 in 2022 with rectangular-screen models at 9.5, 3.0 and 1.9 stellar radii per day, and the speed profiles: slow screens (3 R*/d, about the 3 au case) fail; the 3-sigma lower limit is 7.05-7.41 R*/d.
NEOWISE shows the 2022 rise of the 3-5 um flux of G4466; TESS shows many short dips only in sector 52 (2022 May-June), not in 2020 or 2024. Grey: a comparison star.

(a) No one of 15,941 random screens makes a dip as deep and narrow as the observed events at 3 R*/d. (b) Blackbody temperature at the occulter orbit for circular orbits, from v/R* and the stellar density.
